P8 DELIVERED at b4ad7d20. Cold review returned 2026-09-17 from a fresh-context agent with no memory of writing the code, and it was NOT the Fable agent originally scheduled: Fable 5.1 usage credits were exhausted (an account-level limit no retry clears), and the review that worked was run by the default model, dispatched as a diagnostic. What made it effective was coldness, not model choice -- recorded, because the branch had scheduled six Fable reviews on the premise that risky slices need a frontier reviewer.

THE BEAD WAS RIGHT ABOUT WHERE TO LOOK. It named two carriers with the 'status is publicly constructible' shape and no pass of their own. NotApplicable's Applicability predicate already had consumer probes. CorpusProfile's identity checksum did not -- and that is exactly where the blocker was, though it arrived by arithmetic rather than by construction: two profiles reading DIFFERENT ARTIFACTS digested to the same checksum (3880428e). One sheet with three columns and two sheets with one column each rendered identically, because framing made every part self-delimiting while leaving the part vector flat and count-free against a variable-arity encodingParts. Three earlier forgery probes had each been reasoned about and passed. Fixed by nesting the digest; both the forgery and a 150+ member injectivity family are pinned, and the missing consumer probes were added.

Three MAJORs from the same review, all fixed: SegmentLink.of never compared from.work to to.work; the Friends receipt reported one sheet's refusals while the profile bound two; refusalsTruncated was a Boolean so 101 and 27,777 bad cells read alike. One finding was DISPUTED and not applied -- refusing a non-monotone Coarsening would refuse Memento, which is cut in reverse; documented and pinned instead.

A SURVIVING MUTANT IS RECORDED, NOT REPLACED, as the bead requires: dropping the nesting while keeping the group tags is injective for today's CellEncoding set, because arity is recoverable from the tag literal. Nesting kept because it does not depend on that property. Also recorded: a first mutant survived because it was unfaithful (carried the new part order), which exposed that the original probe pinned an instance and not the invariant -- the reason the injectivity family exists.

Evidence record corrected on three counts it had WRONG, none weakened to match the code: MementoIntake printed no admission line (line added instead); 'ten files' was an uncounted guess (it is seven, now enumerated); 'provably agree' overstated a test that compares Python to Python and never reads SherlockSceneCoding.scala (cross-language agreement remains unpinned). A fourth defect found by the same review: participantPattern was declared, assigned by configure(), and read by NOTHING -- a declared knob that looks live and is inert, inside the contract built to remove exactly that. Now load-bearing with mutation tests.

GATE, command derived from tools/reference-scope.sh against merge-base 0df1d9e7 and pasted not retyped (SD2): exit 0, 24 of 24 modules reporting totals, 2466 tests, 0 failed, 0 errors. scalafmtCheckAll run LAST and separately, exit 0. 7/7 recall-study Python tests pass. Caveat recorded rather than smoothed: one corpusNative compileIncremental failure appeared during a full-tree run after mutation-testing cleans and did not reproduce; that is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis.
